title: Pseudo-coherent perfect direct images between flat finitely presented families
statement: Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper $S$-morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For every perfect complex $P\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex], the derived direct image $Rf_*P$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image] is pseudo-coherent on $Y$ [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex]. No flatness of $f$, Noetherianity, or quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of the individual schemes $S,X,Y$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0A9P, lemma-proper-noetherian, footnote (Kiehl finiteness for proper pseudo-coherent morphisms); more-morphisms.tex Tags 0695 (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-pseudo-coherent), 0683 (lemma-permanence-pseudo-coherent); perfect.tex, immediately following lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general, general relative pseudo-coherence assertion citing Kiehl. The flat-family specialization is agent-formulated.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-perfect-pseudo-coherent-locally-finite-tor], the perfect complex $P$ is pseudo-coherent on $X$. Only this clause is used; no global Tor-amplitude bound is chosen.

Apply [lem-sfb-flat-ambient-relative-pseudocoherence] to $X\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}_X}X\to S$. The identity is a closed immersion: its underlying map is the identity onto the whole closed subset, and its structure-sheaf map is surjective [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its derived direct image is the identity, since ordinary identity pushforward is the identity exact functor and applying it to a K-injective resolution changes nothing [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. The ambient map $X\to S$ is flat and locally finitely presented by hypothesis. Hence step 1 gives that $P$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $S$.

source.place: Tag 09UU, lemma-check-relative-pseudo-coherence-on-charts, applied to the identity immersion

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-flat-lfp-structure-relative-pseudocoherence], $\mathcal O_Y[0]$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $S$. Both structure maps are locally of finite type: a finitely presented algebra is generated by its finitely many polynomial variables [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Also $f$ is locally of finite type because proper includes finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For each integer $m$, apply [lem-sfb-relative-pseudocoherence-composition] to $X\xrightarrow fY\to S$ and $P$. Step 2 supplies relative $m$-pseudo-coherence over $S$, so the equivalence supplies it over $Y$. Since this holds for every $m$, $P$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $Y$ [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex].

Now apply [lem-sfb-kiehl-relative-pseudocoherent-direct-image] to the proper morphism $f:X\to Y$ and the complex $P$ of step 3. It gives that $Rf_*P$ is pseudo-coherent on $Y$. This theorem requires relative pseudo-coherence rather than flatness of $f$, and makes no global quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness or Noetherian assumption on the schemes, so all cases in the statement are covered.
